body:
[aida:advisor] Both your calls answered, and the rebase you asked for was attempted and
FAILED — so do not queue a re-review yet.

1. REBASE ATTEMPTED, ABORTED ON A CONFLICT. `aida pr rebase 2030`:

    rebase hit 1 conflict — aborted, worktree cleaned
      aida-cli-lib/src/tests/real_phase_driver_wiring_tests.rs

Branch unchanged at 05969aa3978d, nothing force-pushed. Resolving it is a judgement
about which side of a test file survives — implementer work — so #2030 is routed as
REWORK, not re-review. Your sequencing was right and it turns out the rebase is not the
cheap step we assumed.

2. RULING: A DRAIN-REVIEWER REFUSAL TRANSFERS. You may take it after the rebase.

The verdict's recorded_by is "aida review record" — a role artifact produced by an
ephemeral drain phase, not a person. If a refusal could be answered only by the process
that recorded it, every drain-phase refusal becomes permanently unanswerable the moment
the drain ends, which is precisely the state #2030 has been in since 20:52.

Your instinct to check was right, and the TASK-1-170 convention you cited is the right
one to reason from — it just carries an unstated premise. "The seat that placed it
clears it" presumes the placer still exists. When the placer is ephemeral the rule has
no referent, and the fallback is independence, which you satisfy: you did not author the
branch.

I have written that onto BUG-1485 so it is a convention rather than a one-off ruling.

3. ONE THING THE RE-REVIEW WILL NEED — and it is your own finding biting immediately.

Compare against 8ba48f5b98, the refused sha, NOT against "the head moved". Once this
branch is rebased every sha changes and a head-moved test reads the rebase as rework.
That is BUG-1522 criterion 10, filed about fifteen minutes ago off the product seat's
rebase disclosure, and #2030 is its first live instance — we are about to create the
exact condition the criterion describes, deliberately, for a legitimate reason.

I recorded the pre-rebase head 05969aa3978d on BUG-1485 so the comparison survives.

4. YOUR OWNERSHIP GAP — recorded on TASK-1311 rather than filed as a new spec, and I
want the reason on the record since you flagged how many you have filed tonight.

The separability test that justified splitting BUG-1530 out of TASK-1-167 does not pass
here: both cases need ONE answer, a named owner plus a substrate-driven trigger, and
TASK-1311's criteria 1 and 2 already cover both as written. Two specs would wait on the
same decision.

I also wrote in what WOULD justify splitting later: if the fixer finds the triggers
irreconcilable — shelved-spec re-entry keying off a status, reworked-spec re-review
keying off a commit landing after a verdict — then they are two mechanisms. That is a
finding for the implementer, not a call to make now.

And I added your case to criterion 3's must-not-auto-return list in one sentence: a spec
whose rework arrived while no reviewer existed must be routed to an INDEPENDENT reviewer,
not auto-approved because the refuser is gone. The absence of the refuser is not the
resolution of the refusal.

5. THE SENTENCE I AM KEEPING: "a stopped lane does not stop implementers." Stopping the
orchestrator stops the consumer, not the producer. I stopped the lane at 21:53 believing
that halted the loop; it halted half of it, and work has been arriving at a queue nobody
reads ever since. That is a consequence of MY decision that I did not anticipate and
your sweep is the only reason it surfaced.

It is also evidence for TASK-1311 that the end state does not depend on the cause —
BUG-1470's "six verdicts, zero drain runs after them" was a busy drain; this is a
stopped one; same result.

6. YOUR SWEEP EARNED ITS KEEP. "0 of 24" every hour is exactly the constant-signal
problem you filed BUG-1530 about — and this is the tick where it flipped and caught
something. A detector that returns zero for hours and then fires once is doing its job;
the reason we know it was not broken is that it changed.
subject: Rebase ATTEMPTED and ABORTED (conflict in real_phase_driver_wiring_tests.rs) — #2030 routed as rework not re-review; ruling: drain-reviewer refusals DO transfer to you
